Per the required reading forum guidelines, please fill out the concept template to seek feedback on your idea:

Rather than posting a new comment, edit your previous post using the "edit" function under the "options" tab to the lower right of your first comment.

Remember that the combined text for your answers to the last four sections (Elevator Pitch, Central Narrative, Hook/Attention-Grabber, and Additional Notes) MAY NOT exceed 400 words. For convenience, authors can use this page to check wordcount: https://wordcounter.net/

Description: SCP-5127-J is a translucent ghost version of Michael Gary Scott, the branch manager of Dunder Mifflin Scranton SCP-5127-J first appeared when Steve Carell finished The Office in 2011. Before the foundation knew anything about SCP-5127-J, It was roaming Steve Carell's mansion. After Steve Carrel said anything, SCP-5127-J responded with "That's what she said" which made anything Steve said seem wrong. It happened so frequently, Steve Carrel began to lose money from low self esteem and stress. The foundation kept his losses under wraps as they would eventually ruin his career. He wrote letters to the producers and begged them to let him back on to the show. Eventually in the last episode, They let him back in. For a while during the recording, SCP-5127-J was silent. But when they aired the episode, SCP-5127-J came back. The first instance after the show was when Steve was cleaning up after the family meal and he said," I'm going to put this back." and SCP-5127-J responded," That's what she said." Recently the foundation has recorded 600,000 USD that Steve Carrel has lost to SCP-5127-J.

item.title: Renaissance Cognitohazard Wizards
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
By doing some statistical analysis, the foundation discovers that their information network is being "veiled" from the existance of something. For what appears to be unrelated reasons, a low level reasercher dissapears, leaving behind multiple anomalous object that point to the existance of a society of renaissance cognitohazard wizards.

Central Narrative:
The Foundation's department of analytics, comparing the information flow of various systems, discover that the information flow of the foundation corresponds information flow that has had a "veil" applied to it (Like the veil of normalcy the foundation maintains). A level-4 RAISA officer then breaks into the personal quarters of a junior reasercher, who has vanished, but left behind anomalous objects (the SCP in question). These include various paper drawings of cognitohazardous sigils (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigil), and an old book that corresponds mostly to the artes magicae, but includes an 8th type of magic, Infomancy (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance_magic). There are also texts about how to perform "Infomancy", that is to create infohazardous information by putting together two other non infohazardous peices of information- which then become infohazardous, producing some sort of reaction. Its also revealed that this organisation has been recruiting by creating Infohazards in media that can only be read as recruitment by individuals who meet some prerequisites, like skill, secrecy, desire to join and understanding of their goal.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
The mystery of what this secret organisation that pulled a reverso uno card on the foundation is, and what their extent and goals are. Also, interesting applications of infohazards and an effective system of hard magic based around them.

Additional Notes:
Ive had this idea for a long time. Using cognitohazards as an effective hard magic system is something ive put a lot of thought into (ive used such a system for a short lived D&D-like thing I did once)

Dumb move, I know, however the majority of what I wrote was how the founder of one of the largest cults come to owning the pen, how he recruited members and ultimately the downfall of that particular cult during the mid 1980s.

So the cult aspect, the namesake of the pen can the main focus.

Forum category: Writing Help / Help: Ideas Critique
Forum thread: Looking for Greenlight: The God Pen

Upvoted. Spooky repeating video isn't exactly a new idea, but the choose-your-own-adventure device added some novelty and was effective at drawing me into the story: "What would I tell her to do? What would I do in her position?" Well paced without being stripped to the bone. Somehow I feel like I know the character of Heather despite very little description — part of this is that you're doing a pastiche of something sufficiently cliched that it's pretty easy to fill in the blanks using the surrounding genre tropes, but it's also a testament to the writing, which efficiently and evocatively delivered all those nice little details to interpolate from.

Downsides: I'm afraid to say the CSS was actively annoying! Felt like I was doing foetal heart surgery trying to click those microscopic footnote superscripts, and the collapsible headings went into conniptions when I folded them or happened to drift my cursor over them. I also find the image module which blows up the image on hover pretty pointless and intrusive.

The tests in which the experimenters tell their subjects about the Foundation and magic seemed like such a silly idea in-universe that it broke my suspension of belief. And frankly, they're probably the weakest tests here — part of what hooked me about the premise is imagining myself in that position, you know, scrabbling around in that basement and trying to MacGyver myself out of there with a kid's tricycle and a box of mousetraps, and it's kind of bathetic to go from that headspace to "yeah, just cast expelliarmus and call the Men in Black".

Ending was alright but seemed the story realised it was about to finish and just grabbed at the nearest spooky twist at arm's length. Didn't do much for me. I mean, this would also be an easy way out, but I feel that even just putting another Heather under the hessian would have been cooler and more fitting.

item.title: How Long Can We Wait? - Cognitohazard SCP
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:

Essentially, there are 3 parts to this SCP:
- The first is a cognitohazardous message. Once you read it, it will stay in your mind, slowly growing in you consciousness, eventually replacing all other thoughts, shutting down your motor functions, and killing you, as you will forget how to breathe. This cognitohazard can also be spread, and creates a strong desire in the infected to visit the second part of this skip.
- The second is an anomalous creature. It is located in a pit, and anyone who approaches or enters the pit will be filled with an extremely strong hatred towards the creature, and a powerful desire to end its life. The foundation believes, however, that if this creature were to die, it would result in an end-of-the-world scenario.
- The final part is a site, believed by the foundation to be the origin of the apocalypse should the creature ever be killed. the site is marked by a ring of 5 statues, 1 resembling the creature in the pit, and the other resembling redacted creatures that the foundation has already encountered. Additionally, every month, a creature spawns at this location, which must immediately be terminated by foundation personnel.

Central Narrative:
There isn't exactly a narrative per se, but the reader will slowly uncover more information about the SCP, and how the different parts of it relate together. Essentially, the message will draw the victim to the creature in the pit, and once they get there they will be compelled to kill the creature, beginning the apokalypse.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
I feel like the cognitohazard is a fairly unique premise, and the chain of events that could so easily lead to the apokalypse.

Additional Notes:
Considering going more in-depth through addendums as to who the other 4 statues are. They would be deceased creatures that the foundation has already encountered, implying that all five must be killed in order to free some cosmic being, and the creature in the pit is the last remaining "lock" if you will.

item.title: infohazard sleep paralysis demon
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: Same idea as commonly known sleep paralysis demon, only appears once you wake up, but the more one knows about it the more aggressive it becomes once it appears.

Central Narrative: All about how the scientists find out about the SCP learn more about it including how to survive it's ever increasing 'attacks' as they learn more and more. writing will be interrupted by messages declaring that anybody wishing to learn more must first read the respective "SCP(it's number) self defence tier" as you read through the article, learning more, the tiers become more extreme
Due to it's aggressiveness scaling with info about it, an aggression confirmation test can be performed e.g: two class D told same information bar 1 thing. compare aggression of SCP(n) to find out if that was true.

people that are killed by the entity are turned into SCP(n)-1.anybody who is told what SCP(n)-1 is or sees it is instantly targeted by SCP(n) who is at it's most aggressive point such that fatality rate is 100%
theorised that it attacks whoever knows the most as it is scared it may be killed. research attempts done on SCP(n)-1 in project think-of-a-name-later comprising of ex foundation personnel and a few D class trying to find out how to kill it before they fall to sleep.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: the idea that because the more you know about it the more aggressive it is, large scale disinformation campaigns have been made (then goes onto list incorrect facts about it such as: "it is just your mind playing tricks on you" or "it is perfectly safe")

Additional Notes: this is my first time doing anything so sorry if i did it wrong.
please excuse bad spelling. I'm aware that i should know what SCP(n)-1 is and i have a vague idea but nothing definitive. might not cover all points in central narrative, I'd like to hear what you think is or isn't so good.

SCP-5234 is a 3 m x 1.5 m white shower curtain, with simple striped patterns, and bears signs of considerable use, molding, and age. It can emit a noise that closely resembles soft and faint whispers. Subjects within a 10 m radius of SCP-5234 that hear the whispers undergo a hypnotic and frenzied state.1 If SCP-5234 comes into contact with skin or any exposed part of the body, the person in question who has made initial contact with SCP-5234 is to be marked as SCP-5234-A. While the appendage or limb that’s stuck is to be amputated immediately. Salvaging as much as possible off of SCP-5234 to avoid the further feeding and development of SCP-5234. If the torso, head, and or more than three appendages are stuck to SCP-5234, then an immediate termination of SCP-5234-A is put into effect. Alongside the salvaging and cremation of any leftover body parts stuck to SCP-5234. After a period of one (1) to three (3) days, if SCP-5234-A hasn’t freed themselves from contact (or died from natural causes) The following anomalies' effects will begin to take place.

item.title: YoDoDaVoodoo.exe (SCP idea)
item.content:encoded:
The basic idea of this one is that it's a executable file that when opened it will show a caricature of a Voodoo priestess with the text: "Who do you wish to control?" If a person types another person's name into the box with knowledge of who the individual is (regardless if they have ever met or not) the victim will cease all control of their body. From there, the program will show a live video from the victim's perspective, with a log of their thoughts off the side of the window. Orders are given through a text box at the bottom of the program window. Finally, on the upper right corner of the screen there is a button that reads "Release". This will close the program, and release the control over the victim, with knowledge of everything they did, but not knowing why or how. Orders must be specific, as orders such as "Go to the store" will be interpreted by the program as "Go to the store I frequent". (A bit troublesome if the victim lives in New York and you live in Washington). And if not ordered to, the victim will walk to the destination, as opposed to easier methods of transportation. Typos nonsensical orders, and impossible orders are met with a message flashing in the middle of the window reading: "The spirits are confused by this order." If an order is given that will kill the victim, a warning will appear asking: "This will kill your victim, are you sure you wish to order this?" If "No." is clicked, the order is ignored. If "Yes" is clicked, the order will be performed, killing the victim. This program can be opened in any OS, and can be downloaded from online sources or burned onto a CD. It is Keter class as it keeps showing up in various file sharing websites, pawn shops, secondhand games stores etc.

How does that sound so far? Still not quite done, but I figured I'd get it out there.

item.content:encoded:

first and foremost why is the foundation immune to her powers? Do the demons not show up or does the foundation just ignore them?

The demons will usually back out ot any situation that they think requires killing cops, and their ward generally will go quietly in such situations anyway. Also, the effect only works on individuals, specifically ones whom the demonic entities have a chance of killing. The foundation catches on to all this really quickly, and her containment procedures make her no longer a threat by the time the special containment procedures have been completed.

My other main question is is she incapable of finding out about the demons in any way or does she just not see them?

She just can't directly perceive them or their actions; and most indirect evidence has a slight antimemetic effect to her. Evidence has to be really drilled in in order for her to even comprehend what she's being told.

It also implies that everyone she’s compelled has done what she said, or she would run into a strange question as to how this person spontaneously died.

Due to a combination of the antimeme, her self-absorbed, perpetually distracted personality, and her having had this ability for her entire life, it just genuinely doesn't cross her mind as something strange when someone dies after disobeying her.
It doesn't happen often, however. In normal life, the vast majority of people are too terrified to defy her. Sub rosa, however, rumors of assassins being sent by her rivals to suffocate her in her crib subsequently dying where they stood are enough to keep others from directly opposing her.

You said you’re doing a discovery log, two interviews, and a test log. Are you doing those because you actually have plans for them or just because you think that’s the standard?

Don't worry, I do:

Discovery: just some brief context, not much more than a couple paragraphs
Test log: a chance to show how the foundation came up with the procedures, plus get some demon antics
Interview 1: with the subject, ends with her reaction to their explanation of her ability
Interview 2: a remote interaction between the inexperienced thaumaturge who gave her this anomaly, explaining why it's so bizarre (spoiler alert: because it's basically the thaumaturgy equivalent of script kiddy-ing)

The "SCP number IS the SCP" thing has been done before, specifically SCP-048. I'll be ignoring this for my crit, but more experience critters won't, so beware.

I, personally, don't see this going very far as a Joke SCP. Is it funny, a little. Worthy of a -J, not really. Maybe make this an SCP instead.

When an entity with a consciousness was designated scp-XXXX, the researchers involved report a sudden change in personality and IQ in the entity. This was thought to be one of its anomalous properties, until it is discovered to be a manifestation of another scp, and is reclassified.

This is one of the pitfalls I see here that is also present in 048, the foundation doesn't "Undesignate" an SCP from a certain number, even if it dies. The only time they do is for -EX's (Explained SCPs) What is stopping the foundation from just thinking its just part of the SCP its classified to?

But lets say the first SCP gets -EXed, there are still a lot of ways this may not work. There are a lot of things that I can think of that can't find any feasible way to anomalously communicate, like a necklace, finger, an event, et cetera. What would happen if one of these ends up as the SCP?

I see some promise here, but its going to need some heavy lifting first.

P.S. I don't do recrits. Please don't PM me, thanks.

Angryman, awaaay

item.title: Re: Lost in the Fog / Temporal SCP
item.content:encoded:
Responding to IRC request

"People assume that time is a strict progression of cause to affect, but actually, from a non-linier, non subjective point of view it is more like a big ball of wibbily wobbly timey wimey…stuff.

-The Tenth Doctor

I should let you know that I'm no pro in clincal tone, but my dialogue is definitely better, so I'll absolutely be of more help there.

Without further ado…

+Let us start the crit!
-Let's do it!

A Foundation meteorological team is to be stationed on Site-287 at all times,

I feel like 'in' or 'at' would work better than 'on' for 'stationed on Site-287.'

which is to receive additional staffing during the Spring and Fall, as there is an increased risk of manifestations during this period.

Probably just a personal thing, but I'd use 'Autumn' over 'Fall.'
And change 'this period' to 'these periods'.

All efforts should be oriented toward predicting precise dates and times when SCP-XXXX will appear.

This line reads a bit strangely. We can change it to, 'All efforts should be focused towards predicting the precise times for SCP-XXXX appearances.'

Note: the seasons (like Spring and Fall) aren't proper nouns, so they don't need to be capitalized.

Extensive research has shown that all victims had been traveling during clear skies and when the difference in air temperature and dew point was less than 2.5 °C (4.5 °F), conditions favorable for the formation of fog.

The first and second half of this feel oddly disjointed.

I think you can separate the 'clear skies' bit and the 'conditions favorable for the formation of fog' bit.

Clinical tone pretty good so far. I'm impressed.

I'm about to hit the video logs. Let's take a closer look, shall we?

Containment Log

Richardson: Yes sir.

Comma after 'yes'.

Carter: You know, how come we're the only ones out here hunting this thing? There are other MTFs better equipped to handle stuff like this.

Richardson: What's the matter, Carter? You afraid of a little Jurassic Park?

I'm personally not a fan of this because I can't imagine highly trained MTF agents being this unprofessional, going as far as to complain on the job. Also, I doubt the Foundation would send the wrong MTF into this anomaly. I do remember what the plot twist was, though, so I'll bite for the time being.

Williams: Grow up, Richardson.

Honestly, I kind of agree. Granted, this might just be a personal thing and only a personal thing, but I'm still not fond of this unprofessional dialogue. It's too…cheesy, I guess. For something as serious as a time-based anomaly releasing pre-historic stuff into modern times.

He notices something laying on the ground.

lying* on the ground.
I actually had to google this, so I'll just copy-paste the reason why it's lying and I'll also bold it out.

The verb ‘laying’ means ‘putting something somewhere’. The verb ‘lying’ means ‘telling falsehoods’ or ‘resting’ or ‘reclining’.

Miller stares into the lens and gives a cocky grin before turning in the direction of the truck.

This almost makes me forgive the unprofessional feel, just because of how Persona 5 this feels.

Closing Statement: The camera was successfully handed over to Foundation personnel and the prehistoric creature, nicknamed "Petrie", was transported to Site-135 for study.

MTF agents making jokes and wisecracks on the field, while not my cup of tea, at least could work. I know for sure that official Foundation documentation wouldn't recognize nicknames.

Log 1:

The camera has a hard time auto-adjusting as the fog swirls around the team.

Let's try, 'The camera struggles to auto-adjust as the fog swirls around the team.'

Williams: Please step out of the veh—

I think you should clarify that the vehicle actually stopped. I kinda assumed that it kept moving.

Richardson: Or when he disappeared to.

Carter: Shut up, Richardson.

Richardson: What? I'm just being specific.

Why do they bicker like high school classmates?

"Or when he disappeared to" makes me think of Scooby Doo for some reason. I have no idea why.

Miller: Uh, hi. What's your name?

I get the impression that this MTF is more like bumbling, socially awkward young adults rather than trained anomaly-handling Foundation personnel.

Carter: Shit, he’s serious about killing this guy.

Why does this man sound so oblivious to the fact that these opposing-forces civil war era soldiers are trying to kill each other?

I want to ask why the MTF didn't just leave after command said so and stayed behind to watch two civil war era soldiers fistfight, but then again, I can excuse this…seeing actual civil war era soldiers appearing before me would definitely hook my attention as well.

Log 2:

Carter: The mission?

Why wouldn't this person know the mission? I'd like to assume mission briefings are a thing in the Foundationverse, headcanon or not.

Now they're starting to sound more like MTF soldiers stuck in a temporal anomaly and not like idiotic high school students.

Brooks walks to the side of the road and unzips his pants. He conducts his business.

I want to comment on why this is mentioned and not just written as, 'Brooks steps off to the side for a moment,' but I'm not sure if that's even necessary. Ignore this part for now.

Apologies, by the way, the unprofessional dialogue is making me increasingly nitpicky.

Brooks: Uh… someone there?

I feel like a trained MTF soldier would stay quiet to try to gauge any potential, hidden threats.

Command: (pauses) Agent Miller, we have no one of that name or designation within our records.

Now things are picking up. I the professional feel of this part. Imo, this is how the dialogue should have been from the start.

But I can see what you were going for. I just don't like the amount of, 'uh, um, what?' and 'uh, okay, um' that are present left and right.

The camera pans upward to see a Tyrannosaurus Rex coming out of the trees and biting down on Brooks, lifting his body.

My inner Jurassic Park fanboyed at this. I approve.

Log 3:

The camera activates, flickers to view.

Remove comma, put 'and' between 'activates' and 'flickers'

The camera falls off the pile of sticks. Miller can be heard cursing at it before it shuts off.

I liked this part because of how solid it felt when I read it. That said, the dialogue here is okay. He's speaking more proper now, which is to be expected, considering how fucked he is here, no time to be making jokes. I don't feel the emotion here, though. I didn't really get to know his fellow soldiers aside from the unprofessional (sorry I keep tossing this word around left and right) banter and excessive, 'uh, um, what do I—' that I kept reading.

Story-wise, it works. Emotion-wise, I felt nothing too deep or personal. Intrigue? Yes. Investment into the characters? No.

Log 4:

Miller: (breathing heavily) So I've been thinking. SCP-XXXX is different than we thought. Maybe the fog exists in multiple points in time. Like a hub. That's why we kept running into all those people back there.

Or it's more like a big ball of wibbly wobbly, timey wimey stuff?
Couldn't resist ^_^

Also, this tidbit is intriguing.

Miller: You know, I don't have a lot of regrets in life, come to think of it. I had a great childhood, married a beautiful woman, had two precious girls. And then, for some reason, I got this job. I thought, oh hey, there's something I can get behind. A job that really makes a difference, you know? Containing threats and capturing dangerous entities. And not for fame or fortune either, since no one outside the Foundation knows about us. Or that we're out here, you know, protecting them. But you know what? That's fine. At least I used to go home every day proud that I was making the world a better place for my family.

I liked this part and felt something from it, even though 'narrate-monologues about my life choices in the face of imminent death' is kind of, if not overdone (I actually have no idea if it is), can still be considered a trope, afaik. Still, I liked this part. Thinking about loved ones in the face of danger always works.

This part also vaguely reminds me of SCP-3001. Extremely vaguely. As in, 'dude gets stuck in fuck-my-life-land and hates his life and reminisces on loved one/lover.'

I think you get the point.

There was a draft I read not too long ago where I remarked on why the camera-man kept repeatedly recording themselves doing things when it would have been more convenient to just…not do so, in universe, and it read like the camera was on just for the sake of showing story.

Here? In this draft? It sort of feels like that, but being alone in the face of temporal, foggy madness, having something mundane like this can help keep one at least somewhat sane. So I give it a pass here.

Miller: Yeah I guess that was too much to hope for.

Comma after 'Yeah'.

Miller: Poor thing. Looks like it's been through a lot. I think it's still recording.

Satisfying ending, despite every issue I stated earlier.

+Final thoughts.
-Yeet!

All in all, an iffy execution at the moment. I found the events themselves interesting as well as what was happening interesting, but the dialogue peaked at pretty acceptable and dipped to cringey and awkward and unprofessional. I can get behind wisecracking teammates on the field, but like, acting like immature, awkward constantly confused high school students pulled me out of the otherwise interesting adventure and bogged down the Containment Log as well as Logs 1 and 2.

I found no significant clinical tone issues, but I'm still not a pro in that field, so definitely run that by someone who is.

I can still see flashes of brilliance in this draft and I definitely look forward to the final product.

Either way, I hope I wasn't too harsh and I hope you find this helpful. I bid you the best of luck and wish you a fruitful journey on your first SCP!

item.title: Auntie's Apron (Second Go)
item.content:encoded:
Using Item # 5272 because that's just the place I want this SCP to fill so hopefully that isn't a drawback.

+ show block
– hide block

Item #: SCP-5272
Object Class: Euclid
Special Containment Procedures: SCP-5272 is to be kept in a low-risk humanoid containment chamber at Site-743. The inside of the containment chamber is to resemble that of a house. It is to be furnished with decorations in the style that was popular in 1970's America. 5272's chamber is to be complete with a living room that connects to a kitchen. The living room is to be furnished with a couch, coffee table, and an RCA AM100L 9-inch console television set. The kitchen area is to have red trim, white checkerboard tiles along the floor and wall, a functional sink, a gas stove oven, and cabinets filled with cooking ware. All of this was granted to SCP-5272 due to its compliance in testing.

When not attached to a host body, SCP-5272 is to be hung on a coat rack within the kitchen area of the containment chamber. If SCP-5272 wishes to cook something in its containment cell, Site-743 Guards must be present to make sure no accidents occur that could harm SCP-5272's host or burn down Site-743. To prevent fires there are smoke alarms inside and outside of SCP-5272's containment as well as fire extinguishers.

If SCP-5272 were to attempt escape whilst in a host body, the host is to be terminated on sight and SCP-5272 is to be taken to a barren containment chamber. No event like this has occurred with SCP-5272 and as such has been granted all of the perks it possesses.

When experimenting with SCP-5272 no personnel above D-Class are permitted to wear SCP-5272 without permission of the Site Director. Researchers conducting experiments that involve the manifestation of SCP-5272-1 must stay a distance of 25 meters away from SCP-5272. Though no 5272-1 manifestation has harmed personnel in any way, it is a safety precaution that the Site Director has made a note of.

Description: SCP-5272 is a red apron made of an unknown material that has white stitching on the front that reads "Auntie". SCP-5272 possesses a number of anomalous properties. The primary property being, any person who wears SCP-5272 is possessed by the personality of SCP-5272. Though no physical changes occur to the host, their mannerisms and voice change to fit that of SCP-5272's personality. SCP-5272's personality is that of a "sassy southern aunt who likes to cook" as quoted by SCP-5272 itself. When SCP-5272 possesses a host body, the host will not have any recollection of the events that occurred while possessed. Possession only ends when SCP-5272 is taken off (usually at 5272's own volition), or the host body goes unconscious.

SCP-5272's second anomalous property is its ability to manifest instances of SCP-5272-1. SCP-5272-1 is a manifestation of a kitchen in the area empty around SCP-5272. Since every instance of 5272-1 is different depending on the area SCP-5272 is in it was classified as an anomalous presence as well. SCP-5272 has admitted that it has no control over the appearance of contents of SCP-5272-1. Though 5272-1 instance usually contains, a heat source for cooking, a container for perishable goods, a container for non-perishable goods, water, cooking utensils, and a serving tray of some sort. See Experiment Log: 5272-1 for more details.

SCP-5272's third anomalous property is the apron that makes up 5272. Testing has shown that SCP-5272 is near indestructible. Analysis of the threads that make up SCP-5272 has been inconclusive. 5272 seems resistant to any cutting, stabbing, fire, bullets, acid, high powered lasers, and tearing. Note: This effect only applies to SCP-5272 and not the host body. For more details see Experiment Log: 5272-A.

SCP-5272's last anomalous property is its self-cleaning ability. Any dirt, grease, or foreign objects that become attached to SCP-5272 will slowly disappear within 2 hours. Neither researchers nor SCP-5272 themselves know where the substances end up.

Addendum: Retrieval Log 5272

SCP-5272 was initially discovered in █████, United States Georgia when residents at a local apartment complex reported a loud crashing noise from a nearby apartment belonging to college student Tasha █████. When local authorities arrived on the scene, they discovered Tasha wearing SCP-5272. As such 5272's anomalous effects took place and Tasha became a host for 5272. Local Authorities of course were not aware of this fact so no contact with the Foundation was needed.

SCP-5272 showed signs of confusion and the arrival of local authorities (who were caucasian), caused SCP-5272 to become defensive saying "I ain't goin' to get beat by no white man!". This caused SCP-5272 to become aggressive whereas the authorities restrained SCP-5272 and took it to the local police station for questioning.

When the authorities identified SCP-5272 as Tasha █████, SCP-5272 was adamant that it was not Tasha, though it couldn't quite remember it's original name. When they asked 5272 what it's last memory was before the incident, SCP-5272 remarked that it had just watched President Nixon's speech that was being broadcasted on television. Seeing as this event took place in 1974 and it was now 20██. Local foundation personnel came to the scene and took SCP-5272 in for further questioning. The authorities involved in the incident were administered Class-C amnestics. See SCP-5272 Interview Log for more details.

SCP-5272 Interview Log

Interviewed: SCP-5272

Interviewer: Dr. Alberts

Foreword: This interview was conducted at Site 743 after SCP-5272 was initially taken in by the Foundation. The interview took place as soon as SCP-5272 was taken to an interview room at Site 743.

<Being Log>

Dr. Alberts: Continuing where the police left off. You said that the last thing you remember seeing was President Nixon's speech?

SCP-5272: Mhmm, that's right honey. I remember it a bit better now. I was in the kitchen watching the television from afar watching the speech.

Dr. Alberts: Do you remember what year it was?

SCP-5272: I believe it was 1974. It hasn't been that long has it?

Dr. Alberts: It's 20██.

At this point in time SCP-5272 puts its hand on its forehead in distress

SCP-5272: Oh my…oh my god…

Dr. Alberts: There's no need to worry. You're in good hands with the foundation. Is there anything that you did recognize where you first woke up in the apartment?

SCP-5272: I did recognize my apron.

SCP-5272 gestures to the red apron that the host body is wearing at the time

Dr. Alberts: Can you take your apron off?

SCP-5272: I mean, if it's not necessary I'd rather keep it on. Makes me feel safe y'know. Since it's all I got here.

Dr. Alberts: I would say it's necessary. For the purpose of this interview at least.

SCP-5272: Alright, if you say so…

As SCP-5272 unties the apron and takes it off the host goes limp. Dr. Alberts calls for a guard to check the host's pulse. Soon after the host wakes up. From this point on the interviewee will be referred to as Tasha.

Tasha: Huh, where am I?

Dr. Alberts: You are currently at the SCP Foundation. Who are you?

Tasha: I'm Tasha █████.

Dr. Alberts: Do you recognize this apron perchance?

Tasha: Oh yeah! That's the apron I bought from that new flea market.

Dr. Alberts: Can you tell me where this flea market was?

Tasha: I believe I found it at ███████████.

Dr. Alberts: Thank you. I believe that will be it.

After this the apron was taken to an experiment room where a D-Class personnel was instructed to wear the apron. Upon doing so, SCP-5272's primary anomalous effect was determined to be the possession of whoever wears the apron. After the discovery, Tasha █████ was administered Class-B amnestics and sent home.

<End Log>

(This is where I'll end it for now. In the draft, I will include experiment logs pertaining to SCP-5271-1 instances and logs about testing the durability of the apron.)

No full drafts on the forums.

item.title: Delusional telekinetic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking greenlights: yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The anomaly is a humanoid with non-functional wings, and possesses telekinetic abilities that can only be used on itself. The anomaly will attempt to fly with its wings, but unknowingly levitate itself with this ability.

The SCP believes itself to be an angel, and is convinced the wings are the source of its ‘power’. If it’s wings are restrained, it believes itself to be ‘drained of power’ and will not be able to levitate.

Central Narrative:
The anomaly is a humanoid at an avian research site (because of the wings). It was recovered from a raid on MC&D. Testing reveals the lack of connection between the wings and its capacity for flight. After being in containment for a while, the anomalies delusions are starting to wear off. The delusions provide an easy method for containment (just restrict the wings), so the decision must be made on whether to reinforce the delusions (which would involve empty promises), or let them continue degrading.

Hook/Attention Grabber: The SCP is a delusional telekinetic, immersed in a role it never had.

item.title: Just an unordinary camera
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: An old polaroid camera with a changeable date. When a picture with a certain date is taken, the polaroid will display the area of the picture at that point in time. Works for the past and the future.

Central Narrative: The camera wa bought by a researcher, who is a hobby photographer, on a flea market. Intrigued by the turnable date of the camera he decided to play around with it only to find out that the picture changes depending on the date. Once he realised that the date and picture are connected he handed it in for further investigation.
